rule: Synapse runner gate members, read from the hook's add_gate_member lines, are exactly the synapse agent type and the five runner scripts
description: plugin/hooks/synapse-gate.sh is the plugin PreToolUse hook that lets hivemind:synapse run the runner scripts with no prompt. Its add_gate_member call lines are what register the one agent type the allow applies to and the runner scripts it knows, so this fixture pins those lines. The set_check captures, from every line that begins (after optional indentation) with add_gate_member followed by whitespace, the whole argument text up to the last non-space character, so each member is the kind and the value together. It requires, in equal mode with expected_counts, exactly these six members, each once: 'agent_type hivemind:synapse' and 'script <name>' for molt, gather-facts, create-working-branch, bump-type and open-plan-pr. An added script or agent type fails as an extra, a changed agent type or a swapped kind fails as an extra and a missing member, a duplicated line fails its count, extra arguments or a trailing comment on a call line fail as an extra, and a deleted line fails as missing. set_check is used because an added member is the threat, and a presence pin can only notice deletion. The capture is the rest of the line, never a charset, so no authored call line can be invisible to it; the function definition line (add_gate_member followed by '()') and the comment that documents it are not call lines and are not captured. The source pin sits on the sentence of the Synapse Runner Gate subsection of plugin/governance/security-policy.md that claims it as the one canonical statement of the gate; deleting that claim is loud. The consumers pin the pointers to it: the '(Synapse Runner Gate)' citation in plugin/agents/synapse.md, and in plugin/hooks/hooks.json the hook's script path and the matcher that routes both the Bash and the Write tool to it, so dropping the registration or narrowing the matcher is loud. What this fixture does not check: (a) members registered any other way, such as a direct write to runner_scripts or gate_agent_type, a call that does not begin its line, a call through a variable, alias or renamed function; (b) what the hook does with its members: the exact-form parsing, the value classes, the deny paths, the inputs-file Write rules and the fail-open behavior are proven by tools/test_synapse_gate.sh, not by this fixture, and the decision prose of the security-policy subsection is human-reviewed; (c) any file not named: files is a literal list naming only the hook, so a second hook file granting synapse anything is unseen; (d) whether hooks.json places the entry under PreToolUse or keeps it in one entry with the matcher; the pins claim word sequences, never structure or meaning.

source.pattern: This subsection is the one canonical statement of the synapse runner gate.
